# P attribute on a virtual rule: the program decides whether the recipe runs,
# called as "prog target prereq", as for file targets.
mk -p 1 -f mkfile -e fresh
stdout 'checked fresh dep'
! stdout 'RAN'
stderr 'mk: fresh is up to date'

mk -p 1 -f mkfile stale
stdout 'checked stale dep'
stdout '^RAN stale$'

# With no prerequisites there is nothing to compare, so the recipe always runs.
mk -p 1 -f mkfile noprereq
! stdout 'checked'
stdout '^RAN noprereq$'

-- mkfile --
fresh:VPsh check.sh 0: dep
	echo RAN $target
stale:VPsh check.sh 1: dep
	echo RAN $target
noprereq:VPsh check.sh 0:
	echo RAN $target
-- dep --
-- check.sh --
echo checked "$2" "$3"
exit "$1"
